speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start at the beginning: can you describe exactly where your pain is located and when it started? To help narrow this down, please tell me if you have any numbness or tingling in your hands or arms. Finally, are your symptoms worse when you raise your arm overhead or when you sleep on that side?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed history; the combination of burning neck/arm pain, paresthesias, and progressive hand weakness in a 58-year-old male is concerning for cervical radiculopathy or a compressive myelopathy. Given your diabetes, I need to know if you have any numbness in your legs or difficulty with balance or walking. REQUEST TEST: Cervical_Spine_MRI

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) with superimposed cervical spondylotic myelopathy. The combination of progressive limb weakness, muscle atrophy (fasciculations), and sensory sparing despite a positive MRI makes ALS the primary concern, while the neck/arm pain and long history suggest a concurrent compressive myelopathy from spondylosis.
